info.title: 🔱Trueno
info.summary: Minimal CGI file host for shared hosting.
info.description: POST a multipart file with a Bearer token, get a short URL back. Each upload chooses a TTL via the `time` field; one option is non-expiring and gets a privileged short URL form. [Trueno](https://github.com/kimari-s/trueno) (MIT) — inspired by [LitterBox](https://litterbox.catbox.moe/) / [catbox](https://catbox.moe/).

bearerAuth.description: Issued out-of-band by the operator; not publicly distributed.

url.description: Public URL. Short-lived buckets carry the bucket as a path segment with a 4-char ID (`/1h/AwkQ.jpg`); the `keep` bucket gets a privileged short form with a 6-char ID (`/AwkqLF.jpg`).

time.description: TTL bucket assigned to this upload.

expires_at.description: Unix epoch seconds when the file is eligible for cron deletion. `null` for the `keep` bucket (no auto-expiry).

post.description: Stores the body under a base62 ID inside the chosen TTL bucket (4 chars for time-limited buckets, 6 chars for `keep`) and returns its public URL. Accepts common images / documents / video / audio / archives (jpg, png, webp, svg, pdf, txt, md, json, mp4, mov, mp3, wav, zip, tar.gz, 7z, …); see `ALLOWED_EXTS` in `_trueno.py` for the full set. Max 50 MiB.

time.description: TTL bucket name. Time-limited buckets are swept by cron; the `keep` bucket is exempt and gets a privileged short URL (no `/<bucket>/` prefix). Allowed values are listed in `enum` above and reflect the runtime `BUCKETS` config.

400.description: Bad request (empty body / missing file field / invalid `time`).

403.description: Bearer token recognised but not authorised for the requested `time` bucket. Per-key bucket allow-lists let an operator hand out a key (e.g., a publicly-shared one) that can write only to time-limited buckets without granting `keep` access.

429.description: Rate limit hit (too many recent uploads in the host-wide window).

get.description: Privileged short URL form, reserved for the `keep` bucket. Apache rewrites this to `/files/keep/{id}.{ext}` and serves the file directly. Not subject to cron expiry, but operator deletion is possible. ID is 6-char base62 — `keep` gets a wider namespace than the 4-char short-lived buckets so URL stability holds across decades of accumulation.

200.description: File body, served directly by Apache.

get.description: Apache rewrites this to `/files/{bucket}/{id}.{ext}`. The file disappears after the cron sweep observes it past the bucket's TTL. ID is 4-char base62 — short-lived buckets accept post-expiry slot reuse, so a smaller namespace is sufficient.

200.description: File body, served directly by Apache.

get.description: Returns the live limits the uploader enforces — server URL, max body size, allowed extensions, TTL bucket choices, default bucket, rate limit, ID length. The LP fetches this on load to populate Swagger UI without requiring a redeploy when these knobs change. Unauthenticated; no key material or upload state is exposed.

web_ui_url.description: Front-end URL the operator advertises for this deployment. Surfaces in the LP via the dynamic Endpoints list so non-developer visitors can find the user-facing site.

ttl_choices.description: Map of bucket name → TTL in seconds, or null for non-expiring buckets.

id_len_by_bucket.description: Map of bucket name → ID character count. Time-limited buckets use a shorter ID; the `keep` bucket uses a longer one so URLs stay stable across decades of accumulation.
